messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Prod error spike detected: prefix-cache layer showing elevated 5xx ~14% (5m) for tenant=acme-corp, route=/generate. Paging maya (oncall).
maya (oncall): Acknowledged. Pulling metrics now. Looks like spike started ~11:22 UTC. Any recent deploys? @deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: No prod deploys in last 30m. Last rollout finished 10:30 UTC.
sam (eng-runtime): I’m seeing a KV latency tail around the same time on host pool-g4-22. Errors correlate with long tail (>350ms) on prefix lookup. Could be a hotkey amplification.
maya (oncall): Good catch. Is this isolated to acme-corp tenant or broader?
ryan (sre): Stack traces show redis timeouts and a small surge of traffic from that tenant. Rate looks like a customer test hitting a long prompt / streaming pattern. Customer support? @anya?
anya (cs): I just chatted with the account. Acme confirmed a heavier-than-usual test at 11:15 UTC, they said they pushed a batch of concurrent requests (not expected to be that large). They're worried about impact; asked if we can limit concurrency.
maya (oncall): For live mitigation we should: (1) apply per-tenant rate cap / concurrency limit for acme-corp, (2) temporarily switch prefix-cache for that tenant to bypass read caching (force fresh lookups) to avoid stale/partial failures if cache lookup failing, (3) if load remains high, enable traffic shaping fallback to a cheaper model. Sam/ryan can you do 1+2? I'll coordinate comms.
sam (eng-runtime): Working on the rate cap now. Will set a soft concurrency cap = 20 and a token/rate cap of 10rps for tenant=acme-corp. Running command:
```
# runtime admin
redwoodctl traffic set-rate --tenant acme-corp --rpm 600 --concurrency 20 --reason "hotkey storm"
```
sam (eng-runtime): Command accepted, policy evaluated, applying to cluster. Propagating in 4 zones.
ryan (sre): I'm going to flip prefix-cache read-through to bypass for that tenant only. This will force direct model-serving lookups and skip prefix index which is currently showing 500s intermittently. Command:
```
redwoodctl cache set-policy --tenant acme-corp --prefix-cache read-bypass --ttl 0 --note "mitigation: bypass prefix cache for correctness"
```
maya (oncall): Give me quick verification steps we can run after change.
sam (eng-runtime): Verify by checking metric acme-corp.prefix_cache.read_success_rate and acme-corp.kv.lookup.latency. Also watch 5xx rate on route /generate. I’ll tail logs.
ryan (sre): Done. Cache policy change pushed in ~15s across the fleet.
sam (eng-runtime): Rate cap applied; concurrent requests for acme dropped from ~120 to ~18 within 20s. 5xx rate falling to ~3%.
maya (oncall): Positive. CS @anya — can you tell the customer we applied a temporary quota/concurrency limit and bypassed some prefix caching to preserve correctness? We should ask them to throttle their test for the next 30 minutes.
anya (cs): Noted. Messaging them now: "We've applied a temporary concurrency and rate limit and toggled cache behavior to reduce errors — you may see slower responses but fewer failures. Please reduce test parallelism and we'll follow up in 30m." :email:
maya (oncall): Monitor for 10m and we’ll reassess. If stable, gradually relax caps and re-enable caching.
sam (eng-runtime): Adding a short-lived selector to route excess traffic to the fallback smaller model (cost-control). Command:
```
redwoodctl routing set-fallback --tenant acme-corp --percent 15 --model small-encoder-v1 --reason "protect cluster"
```
sam (eng-runtime): Fallback set. Observing about ~12% of their requests now hitting small-encoder-v1, which keeps latency <200ms.
ryan (sre): Also putting an alert suppression on the noise for 30m so we don't get paged repeatedly while we're mitigating.
maya (oncall): Good. Anyone see any collateral impact on other tenants?
sam (eng-runtime): No; node-level CPU and memory stable after caps. Other tenant p95 latency unchanged.
maya (oncall): OK plan: monitor 10m, if 5xx <1% and latency acceptable, we will remove the prefix-cache bypass and slowly lift concurrency caps. If 5xx persists, escalate to model-team for deeper investigation into cache backend.
anya (cs): Acme acknowledged, will pause their load and report back once they restart. They asked for ETA to fully restore — can we promise 30min?
maya (oncall): Tentative 30m assuming no regression. I'll update if we need more time.
sam (eng-runtime): Logging steps in incident tracker and will attach metrics graphs. Also saving commands used so we can revert:
```
# revert commands (if stable)
redwoodctl traffic remove-rate --tenant acme-corp
redwoodctl cache set-policy --tenant acme-corp --prefix-cache read-through --ttl 3600
redwoodctl routing remove-fallback --tenant acme-corp --id <generated>
```
maya (oncall): Handing to ryan for next 30m watch. If anything spikes, page me. Handoff: maya -> ryan. @ryan you're the active owner.
ryan (sre): Taking over. I'll post a summary in 30m and update incident status.
maya (oncall): Thanks team. :thumbsup:
anya (cs): Customer says after pausing test, error rate dropped to near 0. They appreciate the quick mitigation. Will keep them updated.
ryan (sre): 30m check-in: metrics stable, 5xx at 0.6%, latency p95 acceptable. I'm going to start relaxing fallback and bump concurrency to 40.
sam (eng-runtime): Concurrency bumped to 40. Reducing fallback percent to 5%.
ryan (sre): Dropping prefix-cache bypass in 2 minutes and watching for errors.
sam (eng-runtime): Re-enabled prefix-cache read-through for tenant acme-corp (ttl 3600). Watching success rates.
ryan (sre): Good — no regression. 5xx steady at 0.4%.
maya (oncall): Thanks. I'll close the pager. Summary: root cause likely hotkey/higher-than-expected concurrent test causing KV tail and cache strain; mitigations were tenant-level rate limiting, temporary cache bypass for correctness, traffic shaping to fallback model. CS notified. Follow-ups: add tenant-level burst-throttles, add autoscale rules for prefix-cache backend, and run a postmortem if recurrence.
incident-bot: Incident resolved and closed by maya (oncall). Duration: 38m. Tags: mitigation, cache, rate-limiting, customer-impact.
